_doc: Italy, Greece, the Adriatic, Turkey and the Mediterranean islands.

destinations.name: Rome
destinations.blurb: Three thousand years of ruins, basilicas and Baroque fountains stacked on top of each other, with the food to match. Relentless in August.

destinations.name: Venice
destinations.blurb: There is nowhere else like it, and everyone knows — which is the problem. Astonishing in February fog, overwhelming in July.

destinations.name: Florence
destinations.blurb: The Renaissance in one walkable square mile — and the gateway to Tuscany's vineyards and hill towns when the queues get too much.

destinations.name: Milan
destinations.blurb: Italy's business and fashion capital: less obviously pretty than its rivals, but unbeatable for design, aperitivo and opera.

destinations.name: Naples
destinations.blurb: Chaotic, operatic and gloriously unpolished — the best pizza on earth, Pompeii and Vesuvius on the doorstep, and prices half of Rome's.
photos: Naples Gulf view Castel dell Ovo

destinations.name: Amalfi Coast
destinations.blurb: Pastel villages glued to vertical cliffs above impossibly blue water. Peerless in May and September; gridlocked and eye-watering in August.
photos: Path of the Gods Amalfi hike

destinations.name: Sicily
destinations.blurb: Greek temples, Arab-Norman churches, Europe's most active volcano and arguably Italy's best food — on an island big enough to need two weeks.

destinations.name: Sardinia
destinations.blurb: Caribbean-grade water on a Mediterranean island, with a fiercely distinct interior of Bronze Age towers, shepherds and mountains.

destinations.name: The Dolomites
destinations.blurb: Pale limestone towers that turn pink at sunset, linked by the world's best ski circuit in winter and via ferrata in summer.

destinations.name: Lake Como
destinations.blurb: Villas, gardens and steep wooded mountains dropping straight into deep blue water — the most theatrical of the Italian lakes.

destinations.name: Cinque Terre
destinations.blurb: Five stacked fishing villages on a vertiginous coast, linked by cliff paths and a train — tiny, gorgeous, and utterly swamped in summer.

destinations.name: Puglia
destinations.blurb: Italy's heel: whitewashed hill towns, conical trulli houses, olive groves to the horizon and two coastlines with barely a high-rise.

destinations.name: Athens
destinations.blurb: The Acropolis floating above a scruffy, energetic, brilliantly cheap city that has become one of Europe's best nights out.

destinations.name: Santorini
destinations.blurb: A drowned volcanic caldera ringed with white-and-blue villages. The most photographed sunset in Europe, and priced accordingly.

destinations.name: Mykonos
destinations.blurb: Whitewashed cubist alleys by day, one of the Mediterranean's most glamorous and expensive party scenes by night.

destinations.name: Crete
destinations.blurb: Greece's biggest island is really a small country: Minoan palaces, a 16km gorge, mountain villages and beaches you can still have to yourself.

destinations.name: Rhodes
destinations.blurb: A complete medieval walled city you can sleep inside, plus a long sunny season and beaches on both a calm and a windy coast.
photos: Palace of the Grand Master Rhodes

destinations.name: Corfu
destinations.blurb: The greenest Greek island, with Venetian and British architecture in the old town and olive groves running down to sheltered bays.

destinations.name: Naxos
destinations.blurb: The Cyclades without the price tag: enormous sandy beaches, a mountainous interior of marble villages, and a working island economy.

destinations.name: Dubrovnik
destinations.blurb: A perfectly preserved walled city rising out of the Adriatic. Walk the walls at dawn, before the cruise ships and the heat arrive.
photos: Mount Srd cable car Dubrovnik view

destinations.name: Split
destinations.blurb: A living Roman palace with bars and flats built into its walls, and the best ferry connections to the Dalmatian islands.

destinations.name: Hvar
destinations.blurb: Lavender fields and hidden pebble coves by day, superyachts and famously messy bars by night — Croatia's most glamorous island.

destinations.name: Istria
destinations.blurb: Croatia's Tuscany: hilltop towns, truffles, olive oil and Venetian harbours, with none of the Dalmatian crush.

destinations.name: Kotor & the Bay
destinations.blurb: A fjord-like bay ringed by mountains, with a walled medieval town and a fortress staircase that earns you the view.
photos: Perast and Our Lady of the Rocks

destinations.name: Albanian Riviera
destinations.blurb: The Ionian coast Greece and Italy already sold: turquoise coves, Ottoman-era Gjirokastër inland, and Europe's last genuinely cheap beach.

destinations.name: Lake Bled & the Julian Alps
destinations.blurb: A church on an island in an emerald lake below a cliff-top castle, with Triglav National Park and the Soča valley behind it.

destinations.name: Malta
destinations.blurb: 7,000 years of history on a limestone rock — megalithic temples, a Baroque capital and world-class diving, all in English.

destinations.name: Cyprus
destinations.blurb: The Med's warmest, longest season — swim into November — with Byzantine mountain churches and Roman mosaics inland.

destinations.name: Istanbul
destinations.blurb: The only city on two continents: Byzantine and Ottoman monuments, a vast bazaar, and ferries criss-crossing the Bosphorus at dusk.

destinations.name: Cappadocia
destinations.blurb: Volcanic 'fairy chimneys', rock-cut churches and underground cities — and a dawn sky filled with a hundred balloons.
photos: Goreme Open Air Museum rock church

destinations.name: Antalya & the Turquoise Coast
destinations.blurb: Roman ruins right on the beach, pine-covered mountains behind, and all-inclusive resorts at prices Western Europe cannot touch.

destinations.name: Bodrum
destinations.blurb: Turkey's smartest resort town — a Crusader castle, whitewashed streets, gulet cruises and a nightlife scene that runs till dawn.
